div.ab: On Cantwarabyrig VII myneteras: IIII þæs cynges ⁊ II þæs biscopes I ðæs abbodes; to Hrofeceastre [III]: II cynges ⁊ I þæs biscopes to Lundenbyrig VIII; to Wintaceastre VI; to Læwe II; to Hæstingaceastre I; oþer to Cisseceastre; to Hamtune II; to Wærham II; [to Dorcaceastre I]; to Execeastre II; to Sceaftesbyrig II; elles to þam oðrum burgum I.

In Canterbury there shall be seven moneyers: four for the king, two for the archbishop, one for the abbot. In Rochester, two for the king and one for the bishop. In London eight; in Winchester six; in Lewes two; in Hastings one; another in Chichester; two in Southhampton; two in Wareham; [one in Dorchester]; two in Exeter; two at Shaftesbury, and one in [each of] the other boroughs.

On Cantwarabyrig VII myneteras: IIII cynges, II bisceopes ⁊ án ðæs abbodes; to Hrofeceastre III: twegen þæs cynges ⁊ an ðæs bisceopes; to Lundenbyrig VIII; to Winteceastre VI; to Læwes II; to Hæstingaceastre I; oþer to Cysseceastre; to Hamtun twegen; to Werham II; twegen to Eaxanceastre; II to Sceaftesbyrig; elles to ðæm oþrum burgum an.
